Office versus Office Group; both options enabled on all four Provider List reports (rule d01).

108 = id of the office the user was working in (legacy correction: the box defaults to the session office, SELECT picks others). Offices (mode office) or office groups (mode office_group); the selection becomes exactly one of office_ids / office_group_id / office_group_ids; tokens working_office, my_offices; all = every office (or group) the caller may read. On this report the office is the provider's roster, not a transaction office: office_attribution = served_office (NEW value, owned by 03 5.1) = overlap of rpt_provider_dim.served_office_ids (provider_offices union home office) with the resolved office set; a provider serving two selected offices is listed under each office band. Which assignment the legacy filter reads (Works At offices assumed) is INFERRED - confirm on the live tool.

Legacy SELECT dialog (dual list with INCLUDE ALL, search, sort) becomes a searchable multi-select; ALL = no restriction; dialog content never captured - confirm list source and whether inactive providers are listed. Role on this report: the listed provider itself (provider_attribution = listed_provider, NEW value for 03 5.2): rpt_provider_dim.provider_id IN (:provider_ids). Not the treating, appointment or preferred provider. The option source lists the roster of the selected offices first, never excludes others (prefer-never-exclude); a picked provider outside the office set returns no row because the office filter still applies.

Lookup-fed dropdown captured collapsed (only ALL known; value list never captured). Options from lookup:specialties (GET /provider-specialties). Filters rpt_provider_dim.specialty, free text, blank on 96 of 97 migrated providers: matched to the catalog value case-insensitively through rpt_value_map domain specialty (NEW, 03 3.7). ALL adds no predicate and keeps providers with a blank specialty; a selected value drops them (null_policy drop). Legacy is single-select; a list is the enhancement. Confirm the list source on the live tool.

Lookup-fed dropdown captured collapsed (only ALL known). Options from lookup:definitions:state (50 states + DC). Filters rpt_provider_dim.state (provider letterhead address state, free text) normalised to the USPS code through rpt_value_map domain state (03 3.7). Which provider state the legacy filter reads (address state assumed, not licence state) is INFERRED. ALL keeps providers without a state. Legacy is single-select; a list is the enhancement.

dynamic_rules.legacy_effect: The SELECT picker chooses office groups defined in Setup > Office Groups (for example regions) instead of offices; when no office groups are defined, a group run covers all offices of the account. Cross-cutting statement of the document for all Lists screens (vendor articles on office groups and on the new reports menu) - recorded once here; it applies to all four Provider List reports.
dynamic_rules.new_behavior: office_scope: the radio value office_scope.mode = office_group switches the picker to lookup:office_groups and the selection fills office_group_id (one group) or office_group_ids (several, enhancement); mode office fills office_ids (default working_office). A group resolves to its member offices intersected with the caller's readable offices. When the tenant has no office groups (every migrated tenant: office_groups is empty) the group mode offers the single value all, which resolves to every office the caller may read - the legacy 'group run covers all offices'. Same behaviour on lists.provider_holidays, lists.provider_operatory and lists.provider_registration (the rule is recorded once, on r01).

legacy_corrections.text: The number in the office box is not a fixed default: with the Office radio the box defaults to the current office (the OID of the session, the same number the title bar shows) and SELECT picks other offices. Recorded once here; it applies to the office box of all four Provider List reports.
